thread:
Sam (Sales): urgent — Acme demo blocked, client sees 413 when sending full conversation + attachments. Demo is tomorrow morning, can we quick-unblock?
Mei (Customer): yep 413 immediate after hitting submit. We're posting a ~6MB JSON payload. No retries, just immediate rejection.
Carlos (Solutions): 413 usually proxy/gateway. Is the error from our endpoint or their infra? Do we have the raw gateway log?
Sam (Sales): gateway log shows response from our public gateway: "413 Request Entity Too Large". client reported ~6.2MB body. Our hosted API usually accepts bigger, so their on-prem proxy might be truncating.
Nina (ML Eng): quick options — for embeddings: split the corpus and send multiple /embeddings calls (one doc per call or small batches). For chat context: compress history — summarize earlier turns into a short system message instead of full history. That cuts tokens a lot.
Mei (Customer): splitting is fine but some attachments are nested inside the JSON (base64). Not trivial to split on client side without extra engineering.
Carlos (Solutions): immediate workaround: 1) try Content-Encoding: gzip to reduce bytes; 2) presign attachments -> upload to S3 and send URLs instead of base64 payload; 3) stream smaller pieces and reassemble server-side. Which can we ship fast?
Jay (Infra): also check NGINX `client_max_body_size` on the customer's gateway. If that's the blocker, nothing on our side will help unless they change config. Streaming/multipart or presign avoids that limit.
Sam (Sales): customer is unlikely to change gateway config before demo. So we need a solution we can deploy quickly or give them a client workaround.
Carlos (Solutions): propose a tiny "splitter" shim script they can run locally: it reads their big JSON, extracts attachments to files, uploads to S3 presigned URLs (we provide), replaces embedded blobs with URLs, and posts the reduced JSON. Can ship today.
Nina (ML Eng): for chat overflow we can also provide a small summary routine (reduce-history) that ingests full chat, returns a compact summary + last N turns. They run it locally before sending. That avoids losing context in the demo.
Mei (Customer): that sounds doable. Any code sample?
Carlos (Solutions): quick sample — run on their laptop: \n```bash\n# split attachments, upload, and post reduced payload\npython tools/split_upload.py --input convo.json --presign-endpoint https://our-presign.example.com | curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d @-\n```\nCarlos (Solutions): or very-short curl to try gzip: \n```bash\ncat payload.json | gzip -c > payload.json.gz\ncurl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Content-Encoding: gzip" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --data-binary @payload.json.gz\n```
Jay (Infra): note — some customer proxies reject Content-Encoding gzip as well (they inspect uncompressed size). Presign + upload is the most robust.
Sam (Sales): perfect. Carlos, can you drop the splitter script + readme into a gist and I'll share with Mei? I'll say this is a temporary demo workaround, we'll follow up with server-side ingestion for production. :thumbsup:
Carlos (Solutions): on it, will paste link in 10m. Also cc Nina for advice on summarization thresholds (how much to trim without losing intent).
Nina (ML Eng): recommend: keep last 3 user/assistant turns + 1 summarized system block. If worried about QA, run a quick eval against a few prompts to confirm.
infra-bot: deploy-check: presign-service reachable (eu-west-1) — OK.
Mei (Customer): thank you everyone — trying presign + splitter now. Will report back in ~20m.
Sam (Sales): thanks team, I'll stay on call with them for the demo.
Carlos (Solutions): gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/splitter-demo-example (contains split_upload.py + README).
Mei (Customer): confirmed — presign + replace worked, payload dropped to ~800KB, chat accepted. Demo looks unblocked. 
Sam (Sales): nailed it, team. I'll follow up post-demo to scope a proper ingestion flow and docs. :party_parrot:
